'''Mary Perry Smith''' (May 29, 1926 – August 10, 2015) was an American mathematics educator who cofounded the [[Mathematics, Engineering, Science Achievement]] program and the [[Black Filmmakers Hall of Fame]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Mary Perry Smith |url=https://www.legacy.com/us/obituaries/eastbaytimes/name/mary-smith-obituary?pid=175507043 |publisher=Inside Bay Area News |access-date=31 August 2021}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Perry Smith was born on May 29, 1926, and was originally from [[Evansville, Indiana]], one of six children of a minister in the [[African Methodist Episcopal Church]]; her maternal grandfather, Henry Allen Perry had been a chaplain and mathematics teacher at the [[Tuskegee Institute]], where her parents met. As a child she moved frequently, to [[Kokomo, Indiana|Kokomo]], [[Logansport, Indiana|Logansport]], [[Anderson, Indiana|Anderson]], [[Crawfordsville, Indiana|Crawfordsville]], and [[Frankfort, Indiana|Frankfort]], all in Indiana. She earned a bachelor's degree from [[Ball State University]] in mathematics and science in three years, as one of a small number of African-American students there, and continued at [[Purdue University]] for a master's degree in counseling and guidance (with minors in biochemistry and statistics), finishing in 1948.{{r|wilmot}}

==Later life and career==
Unable to find a job because of the discrimination in teacher hiring in Indiana, she followed her older brother to the newly opened [[Texas Southern University|Texas State University for Negroes]] in Houston, where she taught mathematics for three years.{{r|wilmot}}

After marrying [[Norvel L. Smith]] (later to become the president of [[Merritt College]] and the first African American head of a college in California) and moving with her husband to [[Oakland, California]],{{r|oac}} she joined a doctoral program in educational psychology at the [[University of California, Berkeley]], but moved to part-time study and then stopped out to become a teacher, first in a junior high school in San Francisco from 1953 until 1961,{{r|wilmot}} and then at [[Oakland Technical High School]], where she taught geometry for 17 years.{{r|wilmot|otc}}

==Service==
In 1969, Perry Smith cofounded the [[Mathematics, Engineering, Science Achievement]] (MESA) program for under-privileged pre-college students in California.{{r|wilmot|oac}} In 1974, she cofounded the [[Black Filmmakers Hall of Fame]] in [[Oakland, California]], initially as part of the Oakland Museum’s Cultural and Ethnics Affairs Guild and, in 1978, as a separate organization;{{r|oac|bfca}} she also served as its president.{{r|ebony}} She left her teaching position to work for the MESA program in 1977,{{r|oac}} as statewide program director,{{r|wilmot}} and also served on the board of the [[Oakland Museum of California]].{{r|oac}} She died in 2015.{{r|oac|bfca}}

==Legacy==
Her papers are kept in the [[Bancroft Library]] of the [[University of California, Berkeley]].{{r|oac|pcia}}
